item.content:encoded:
Pacific foreign ministers gathered in Suva, Fiji today to discuss regional priorities ahead of the 55th Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting ( PIFLM55 ) in Palau later this month. Tonga was represented at the meeting by HRH Crown Prince Tupouto'a 'Ulukalala, Minister for His Majesty's Diplomatic Services ( HMDS ).

The meeting took place amidst heightened geopolitical interest in the region.

The chairman, Minister of Foreign Affairs and External Trade, Solomon Islands Hon. Rick Houenipwela, urged the critical need for the forum to remain united.

" There has never been greater international interest in our region. There has never been greater demand for Pacific engagement. And there has never been a more important time for the Pacific Islands Forum to remain united around our priorities," he said.

He stressed that partnerships are important, but the Pacific agenda must be shaped and owned by the region itself.

" As foreign ministers, we have a unique responsibility. We sit at the intersection of our domestic priorities and collective regional interests. We help shape how the Pacific engages the world, manages its partnerships, and protects the integrity of our regional institutions. That responsibility extends beyond today's agenda. It is about ensuring that in an increasingly contested international environment, the Pacific continues to engage from a position of unity, purpose, and strategic confidence."

Meanwhile, PIF Secretary-General Baron Waqa reminded the leaders that the "Pacific Way" will continue to guide their efforts.

" The principle of the Pacific Way that has guided the Pacific Islands Forum more than five decades, remain unchanged."

" On my part, allow me to reaffirm that the Secretariat remains committed, to supporting a forum that is increasingly strategic, responsive, and implementation focused. One that is able to anticipate emerging challenges, coordinate regional action and deliver effectively on the priorities set by leaders," said Waqa.
